From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: production errors - MerchantCo (URGENT customer escalation)

Triage notes (initial):
- Observed region: us-west-2 (AZ a/b) starting 08:47 PST; cluster p95 token latency jumped from ~210ms to 1.8s.
- Error class: transient 502/504 tied to KV cache thrashing and accelerated retry amplification; autoscaler shows worker churn and repeated model reloads.
- Cause hypothesis: a sudden shift in long-sequence requests from MerchantCo (their new batch job) with higher-than-normal sequence lengths + high concurrency caused KV cache eviction pressure; combined with a small regression in kernel path for our quantized runtime on a subset of instances.

Immediate recommended mitigations (actionable):
1) Route 20-30% of MerchantCo traffic to us-east-1 (canary) for 15 minutes. Monitor p95 and error-rate delta.
2) Increase KV caching window for MerchantCo on west-2 (config change) to reduce evictions; this requires a minor runtime flag flip (non-disruptive).
3) If canary shows improvement, gradually shift to 100% in 30m.
4) If errors persist, apply emergency fallback: pin MerchantCo to the latest stable model variant on dedicated pool (requires exec permission for priority pin).

Attachments: I pulled recent traces and a 10-minute p95 extract (p95_latency_log.txt) — contains timestamps and kernel-level errors.

Risks: cross-region steer may hit higher tail latency for other customers if their routing is dependent on west-2; network ACLs and VPC peering for MerchantCo are validated but we should notify their infra. Also a priority pin/eviction of other customers is a heavy hammer and requires leadership sign-off.

I'll start canary routing once Tessa confirms and Ops gets sign-off from account/leadership for the pin if needed.

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt | Senior SRE, Routing & Serving
Redwood Inference

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: URG: MerchantCo telemetry 5xx + latency spike — mitigation summary

Summary (closing update):
- Canary: 25% traffic to us-east-1 at 11:25 PST. Within 8 minutes p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 260ms and error-rate from 18% -> 1.6%.
- Full failover: we completed a 100% handoff to us-east-1 at 11:40 PST; errors returned to baseline and order flow resumed.
- Root cause (preliminary): KV cache eviction amplification combined with a narrow subset of older kernels in west-2 under higher sequence-length workload. Ops applied a runtime flag to enlarge MerchantCo's KV window and queued a kernel patch (scheduled out-of-band).
- Customer impact: orders resumed; no data loss reported. MerchantCo requested a postmortem and commercial remedy.

Follow-ups:
1) Postmortem doc (Confluence) and JIRA INC-9921 assigned for kernel regression + runtime flag audit.
2) Recommend 10% one-time credit; Marissa to confirm final commercial language.
3) Ops will run a west-2 CV to validate kernel patch and will prepare a low-risk backfill to return MerchantCo to west-2 in steady state.

Thanks all for quick response. I'll send the incident timeline and a short exec one-pager.

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt | Senior SRE, Routing & Serving
Redwood Inference
